To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
oak forest regeneration can only succeed if the competitive pressure from other tree species is reduced, if the regeneration area is fenced and if the competitive vegetation is removed.

the most important factors that determine the success of oak forest regeneration are the absence of competition from other tree species, fencing, and the absence of competition by vegetation (weeds and grass).
the absence of competition, fencing and the retention of habitat trees are the most important success factors for the regeneration of high-quality oak stands in northwest Germany.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a holistic approach to oak regeneration planning, which considers both the economic and the ecological aspects.
the development of an efficient and sufficiently robust sampling design and a Bayesian statistical modeling procedure for analyzing the crucial success factors of high-quality oak forest regrowth.
the identification of crucial factors for successful oak regeneration and the development of a methodological basis for the efficient planning of oak regeneration within a forest enterprise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a high-quality oak forest stand regeneration can be achieved by combining the following measures: a) the retention of habitat trees and a careful regeneration planning; b) the use of fencing; c) a careful pre-commercial thinning; and d) the avoidance of competition from other tree species.
oak regeneration is a very demanding and time-consuming task.
the success of oak forest regeneration is mainly determined by the competitive pressure from secondary tree species, the absence of fencing, and the absence of weeds, grass, and bracken.

the success of oak forest regeneration is mainly influenced by the competitive pressure from the surrounding vegetation and the presence of fencing, which can be influenced by forest management measures.
oak regeneration planning should be done in a very careful way, taking into account the ecological and economic demands and the site conditions.
the success factors identified here should be taken into consideration when developing oak regeneration strategies in the future.

oak regeneration is a long-term investment, and that a successful oak regeneration requires a long-term perspective and a lot of time and money.
